title: Build the counter layout
objective: Render a reusable counter before introducing changing state.
tasks: Add a controls div containing five native buttons: -100, -1, Reset, +1, +100.
Keep the displayed value at zero and render Counter inside App.
Check that all five controls are visible and keyboard focus reaches them. They intentionally do nothing yet.
hints: Use className="controls" for the supplied layout.
Keep the value in an output element; changing values comes in the next lesson.

title: Make the counter interactive
objective: Use local React state to connect the five counter controls.
tasks: Import useState and initialize value to zero inside Counter; render value instead of the literal zero.
Wire ±1 and ±100 using functional updates so repeated clicks accumulate.
Make Reset set the value to zero. Try +100, -1, Reset, then -100.
hints: An event handler is a function: onClick={() => setValue(current => current + 1)}.
Reset replaces state; incrementing derives the next state from the previous value.

title: Create an observable counter store
objective: Move counter behavior into a class with observable state and bound actions.
tasks: In the constructor call makeAutoObservable(this, {}, { autoBind: true }).
Implement add as an accumulating action. Ignore non-finite deltas and results instead of storing NaN or Infinity.
Implement reset and verify the same five controls. Read why the supporting App still copies the store value into local state.
hints: Compute const next = this.value + delta, then use Number.isFinite on both delta and next.
autoBind keeps reset safe when passed directly as an event callback. makeAutoObservable does not subscribe a React component.

title: Subscribe React with observer
objective: Render observable values without a duplicate local-state snapshot.
tasks: Wrap Counter in observer from mobx-react-lite, keeping its counter prop.
Read counter.value during the observed render and leave actions on the store.
Check +100 then -1 displays 99, and Reset works without calling a React setter.
hints: Use const Counter = observer(function Counter(...) { return ...; });.
The starter changes the model on click but has no render subscription. Wrapping only App would not track reads inside the unwrapped Counter.

title: Manage multiple counters
objective: Compose observable counter instances in an observable parent collection.
tasks: Implement Store.addCounter: stop at safetyLimit, then push new CounterStore(this.nextId++).
Replace the single Counter with a map over store.counters and use counter.id as its React key.
Add several counters, change each independently, and confirm resetting one does not change the others.
hints: The supplied parent App is an observer because it reads the observable list. Each Counter is also an observer because it reads its own value.
IDs are assigned once and excluded from observation. The temporary safety limit of 20 prevents an unbounded teaching preview; the next step adds a four-counter business rule.

title: Derive capacity and the total
objective: Use computed getters for the four-counter limit and sum.
tasks: Derive canAddMoreCounters from counters.length and limit, then use it inside addCounter.
Derive sum with reduce over all counter values; do not store a separately maintained total.
Add up to four counters. Confirm Add counter becomes disabled and changing or resetting any counter updates the total.
hints: makeAutoObservable turns getters into computed values. Return this.counters.length < this.limit.
The disabled button is feedback; the guard in addCounter enforces the same rule for every caller.

title: Remove a counter safely
objective: Remove by stable identity while derived state updates automatically.
tasks: Implement removeCounter with filter, excluding the supplied ID and retaining the other instances.
Fill all four slots, assign different values, and remove a middle counter. Check the remaining IDs and values.
Verify capacity and total update, add a new counter, then remove all counters and recover using Add counter.
hints: Assign this.counters = this.counters.filter(counter => counter.id !== id).
Do not renumber survivors or reset nextId after removal; identity is separate from array position.

title: Restore and serialize URL state
objective: Hydrate validated values and synchronize them with the URL using a disposed reaction.
tasks: Implement serializedValues as a semicolon-separated value list and hydrate as an all-or-nothing validated replacement.
Reject more than four counters, payloads longer than 512 characters, blank tokens, NaN and Infinity. Treat an entirely empty string as an empty collection.
Implement restoreUrl and syncUrl. Use the value query parameter, preserve other parameters and the hash, catch browser failures, and return the reaction disposer.
Load 5;-2, change a value, and inspect the share query. Invalid input such as 1;;2 or Infinity must preserve the current collection. In the exported app, reload a URL containing ?value=5%3B-2.
hints: Validate all tokens first; only then map them to new CounterStore(this.nextId++, value) instances.
reaction(() => store.serializedValues, value => {...}, { fireImmediately: true }) returns a disposer. The supplied React effect returns it on unmount.
Use new URL(window.location.href), url.searchParams.set, and history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", url), inside try/catch.

title: Persist counters in localStorage
objective: Restore validated browser data and dispose both URL and storage synchronization.
tasks: Complete connectPersistence: a valid URL has priority, otherwise restore a validated JSON number array from STORAGE_KEY.
Catch storage access and JSON errors. Reject non-arrays, more than four items, oversized JSON, non-number values and non-finite numbers.
After restoration, use autorun to save only a plain array of counter values; catch quota or blocked-storage errors.
Return cleanup that stops both effects. Verify empty arrays, malformed JSON, URL priority and restoration after removing the value query parameter.
hints: JSON.parse returns untrusted data: assign it to unknown, then narrow with Array.isArray and an every check. Reuse store.hydrate only after validation.
autorun runs immediately. Restore first so a default snapshot cannot overwrite the saved values before they are read.
Keep storage and URL effects inside connectPersistence, called by the supplied useEffect. Return both disposers; do not start an autorun at module scope.
